decisions.summary: row 14's fix 'Ubame's 19 cut to that rule' dropped: the plan says Ubame's 19 tubs for its ~19 wooden buildings already follow the rule, and the claim is restated to assert it
decisions.why: the accepted ranked fix (FR-001) says cut Ubame's 19 to one per major wooden building plus two at the kitchen; the plan drops the cut on a premise nobody measured - m:wave99-tubs-and-pillars records Ochiba's count and the pillars, nothing on Ubame's buildings or its tubs per building, and '~19' is the sheet's own old note. Measured on the sheet (identical at HEAD): the west residence wing (residence-2) carries two tubs on one face, (246,256) and (246,290), and the east wing (residence-5) two, at (537,232) and (844,310), while the rule gives two only to the kitchen; several wooden buildings carry none. Nothing makes the cut impossible, the request does not imply it, and the row's purpose is the one-per-building placement. Measure Ubame's buildings and tubs per building into the record, apply the rule, and put any 'a long wing takes two' through a MODE 1 exception check as a labeled deviation, not as the rule.

decisions.summary: row 14 taken ahead of the row it depends on: a tub added at Ochiba's karo's house while E3 row 21 ('senior retainers housed apart': karo's house removed from inside the walls, Ochiba, Hayakawa) stands open
decisions.why: row 14's 'after' names row 21 and its fix says 'a tub added at Ochiba's karo's house / senior retainers' quarters (if they survive)'; 328's FR-003, carried by 372's FR-001/FR-002, requires a row to follow any row it depends on. The plan neither records the order break nor measures whether the buildings survive; row 21's fix removes the karo's house the new tub serves. Nothing made row 21 impossible first (no hold flag on it). Take row 21 first, or hold row 14's Ochiba half until it lands, and record the order in the plan.
